Hi Sam / ACME team,

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so your security team can triage:

Summary / next steps
- Redwood confirmed we can support ACME's requirements around audit logging, data residency, and evidence for vendor security review.
- Requested: vendor security questionnaire (attached), plus a technical session to review logs/export options.

Questions for your security/compliance team (high priority)
1) SOC 2: Do you require a current SOC 2 Type II report for procurement, or is Type I + roadmap acceptable temporarily?
2) HIPAA/GDPR: Are there any special controls or data flow diagrams you need beyond the questionnaire?

Audit logging capabilities (please see attached matrix) — high-level answers below; Dev is looped for deeper tech details:
- Admin activity logs: All admin actions are audited (actor, timestamp with TZ, IP, action, resource path).
- API logs: We capture API request metadata (requester id, endpoint, request size, response status, latency) and, by default, do not store full request/response bodies unless customer enables structured request-logging for troubleshooting.
- Exportability: Logs are exportable via our logs API in JSON or CSV, can be streamed to customer S3 buckets or pushed to syslog/Datadog via a secure connector.
- Immutability: Logs are stored in an append-only audit store; exported archives can be marked WORM and we maintain signed digests for tamper-evidence.
- Retention & deletion: Default retention is 365 days for audit logs; configurable per-customer from 30 days up to multi-year (with export options).

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 overview), audit-logging-matrix.xlsx (fields/exports).

Action items
- Sam: confirm whether ACME requires SOC 2 Type II now or if Type I + timeline is acceptable.
- ACME: share the vendor security questionnaire (or confirm the attached template is what you need).
- Dev/Aditya: follow up with technical session times (I propose next Tue/Wed morning PST).

Thanks — I will draft answers for the vendor SQ once you share it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions

Thanks Marissa — appreciated. A couple of quick clarifications from our side:

1) SOC 2: Our procurement policy prefers a current SOC 2 Type II report. If you have a Type II report from the last 12 months, that will speed approval. If not, we can accept Type I plus an explicit timeline for Type II as a stop-gap for the pilot.

2) HIPAA/GDPR: We're particularly focused on PII access controls and data subject deletion proofs. Can you confirm whether audit logs capture data deletion events and the actor who initiated them?

3) Logs & SIEM: We typically request logs to be streamed into our SIEM (Splunk). Can you confirm whether streaming to S3 + our ingestion process is supported and whether logs include full request IDs to correlate with traces?

Attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire — please return with answers and any supporting evidence. Also include a technical contact for a deeper session (we'll need someone who can walk the schema and examples).

Sam

Hi Sam — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. I've attached our first-pass answers (acme-sq-answers-v1.pdf) and below are short answers to your bullets while we confirm details with Dev/Aditya: 

SOC 2
- Status: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report (issued 2026-11-01). Public summary attached (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). Full report available under NDA; we can provide a copy to ACME legal once we have an NDA in place.

Audit logging specifics (summary)
- Admin activity logs: Yes — every admin/change is logged with user identity, timestamp, IP address, action, and resource identifier. Logs include the admin UI action and API-based admin calls.
- API logs: Metadata for every API request (caller id, endpoint, timestamp, latency, response code). Full request/response bodies are not retained by default; however, customers can enable structured debug logging for specific jobs which captures request/response payloads for a limited retention window.
- Export & streaming: Logs can be exported via our Logs API (JSON/CSV) and we support direct delivery to customer S3 buckets and secure syslog/HTTPS ingestion endpoints. We include request IDs for trace correlation.
- Immutability: Logs are stored in an append-only store with signed digests to provide tamper-evidence. For long-term archives, we support WORM-enabled S3 buckets on export.
- Retention: Default 365 days, configurable up to multiple years. Deletion events are recorded in the audit stream (actor, timestamp, resource id).

Technical contact & next steps
- Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwood.ai) will run a short technical session to walk the log schema and show export examples. Aditya will coordinate access to SOC 2 evidence under NDA.
- Proposed session: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 at 09:00 PST — does that work for your team?

I've attached the first-pass questionnaire answers; we'll iterate quickly once you flag any gaps.

Thanks,
Marissa
